literal: The officials memorialized that state revenue was insufficient and firmly requested restoration; only Su said:
idiomatic: The officials memorialized that state revenue was insufficient and firmly pressed to restore the levies; only Su said:

literal: "I have heard that when the people lack sufficiency, with whom shall the ruler have sufficiency?"
idiomatic: "I have heard that when the people lack sufficiency, with whom shall the ruler have sufficiency?"

literal: The emperor approved and followed him.
idiomatic: The emperor approved and followed his counsel.

literal: Su was a paragon among the imperial clan and also advanced in years; the emperor each time summoned him in to consult on state affairs, yet he firmly declined illness and returned home.
idiomatic: Su was a paragon among the imperial clan and also advanced in years; the emperor repeatedly summoned him to consult on state affairs, yet he firmly pleaded illness and returned home.

literal: By nature upright, in office fifty years, beginning and end as one—the age judged him worthy.
idiomatic: Upright by nature, he held office fifty years with beginning and end as one—the age judged him worthy.

literal: He died; posthumous title Kang, buried with honor at Jinling, enshrined in the ancestral temple.
idiomatic: He died; posthumous title Kang, buried with honor at Jinling, enshrined in the ancestral temple.

literal: The eldest son Kesiling, at seventeen, followed Emperor Taiwu on the hunt, pursuing a fierce beast; Ling thereupon wrestled it bare-handed and presented it.
idiomatic: The eldest son Kesiling, at seventeen, followed Emperor Taiwu on the hunt, pursuing a fierce beast; Ling thereupon wrestled it bare-handed and presented it.

literal: The emperor said, "Your talent and strength are unmatched—establish merit and achievement for the state; do not act thus!"
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your talent and strength are unmatched—establish merit and achievement for the state; do not act thus!"

literal: He was at once appointed Inner Attendant A'gan.
idiomatic: He was at once appointed Inner Attendant A'gan.

literal: Again he followed in the pacification of Liangzhou; Juqu Maoxian ordered a fierce general to engage Ling in combat—both spears broke; Ling drew an arrow, shot him, and he fell from his horse.
idiomatic: Again he followed in the pacification of Liangzhou; Juqu Maoxian ordered a fierce general to engage Ling in combat—both spears broke; Ling drew an arrow, shot him down, and he fell from his horse.

literal: Ling feared rescue would arrive; before he could draw his sword he used his knife to lever the man's neck and sever head from body.
idiomatic: Ling feared rescue would arrive; before he could draw his sword he used his knife to lever the man's neck and sever head from body.

literal: The emperor admired him; that same day he was made Commander of the Capital Garrison and enfeoffed Marquis of Jiyang.
idiomatic: The emperor admired him; that same day he was made Commander of the Capital Garrison and enfeoffed Marquis of Jiyang.

literal: He died as Commander of the Central Army.
idiomatic: He died as Commander of the Central Army.

literal: The younger brother Peijin inherited the title; for an offense the fief was abolished.
idiomatic: The younger brother Peijin inherited the title; for an offense the fief was abolished.

literal: Peijin's son Zhao, childhood name A'ni, was by Zhang Yi of the Secretariat introduced as acting Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: Peijin's son Zhao, childhood name A'ni, was by Zhang Yi of the Secretariat introduced as acting Palace Attendant.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen was to hold mourning for Prince of Qi Commandery Lan, yet Zhao composed palace music instead.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was to hold mourning for Prince of Qi Commandery Lan, yet Zhao composed palace music instead.

literal: The emperor was greatly angered and said, "A'ni is stupid and dull—who introduced him as attendant?"
idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered and said, "A'ni is stupid and dull—who introduced him as attendant?"

literal: Thereupon Yi was demoted to commoner to guard the Secretariat, and Zhao was stopped and dismissed.
idiomatic: Thereupon Yi was demoted to commoner to guard the Secretariat, and Zhao was stopped and dismissed.

literal: Under Emperor Xuanwu, Zhao's cousin Hui was favored and wielded power; he was gradually promoted to Left Assistant.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu, Zhao's cousin Hui was favored and wielded power; he was gradually promoted to Left Assistant.

literal: When Xuanwu died, Yu Zhong held power; Zhao became Yellow Gate Attendant and again curried favor with him.
idiomatic: When Xuanwu died, Yu Zhong held power; Zhao became Yellow Gate Attendant and again curried favor with him.

literal: Zhong monopolized authority and abused power, wrongfully entrapping the loyal and worthy—much was at Zhao's instigation.
idiomatic: Zhong monopolized authority and abused power, wrongfully entrapping the loyal and worthy—much was at Zhao's instigation.

literal: When Empress Ling held court, he was made Minister of the Secretariat and Intendant of Henan—deaf, fierce, and harsh; affairs were stern and urgent; wherever he went, men suffered.
idiomatic: When Empress Ling held court, he was made Minister of the Secretariat and Intendant of Henan—deaf, fierce, and harsh; affairs were stern and urgent; wherever he went, men suffered.

literal: Soon he went out as Inspector of Yong Province; in the province he was greedy and cruel, greatly harming people.
idiomatic: Soon he went out as Inspector of Yong Province; in the province he was greedy and cruel, greatly harming people.

literal: Later he entered again as Minister of the Secretariat and flattered Liu Teng.
idiomatic: Later he entered again as Minister of the Secretariat and flattered Liu Teng.

literal: He was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West.
idiomatic: He was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West.

literal: He died; posthumously Minister of the Secretariat Left Deputy.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously Minister of the Secretariat Left Deputy.

literal: He bribed Yuan Cha—therefore the posthumous gifts were exceptionally generous.
idiomatic: He bribed Yuan Cha—therefore the posthumous gifts were exceptionally generous.

literal: Zhao's younger brother Shao, styled Choulun, was clever from youth.
idiomatic: Zhao's younger brother Shao, styled Choulun, was clever from youth.

literal: He was promoted to Right Assistant of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Assistant of the Secretariat.

literal: Emperor Xuanwu ordered him to examine Zhao Xiu's case; because Xiu was a favorite, Shao therefore added cane punishment and ordered his death.
idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu ordered him to examine Zhao Xiu's case; because Xiu was a favorite, Shao therefore added cane punishment and ordered his death.

literal: The emperor reproached Shao for not reporting again; Shao said, "Xiu's treachery and flattery exceed Dong Xian's—I if I did not seize the occasion to remove him feared Your Majesty would again bear the name of Emperor Ai."
idiomatic: The emperor reproached Shao for not reporting again; Shao said, "Xiu's treachery and flattery exceed Dong Xian's—if I did not seize the occasion to remove him, I feared Your Majesty would again bear the name of Emperor Ai."

literal: Because his words were correct, he was not punished.
idiomatic: Because his words were correct, he was not punished.

literal: On leaving, Prince of Guangping Huai bowed to Shao in congratulation, saying, "Sir, you are the clan's integrity—even Zhu Yun and Ji An cannot be looked up to!"
idiomatic: On leaving, Prince of Guangping Huai bowed to Shao in congratulation, saying, "Sir, you are the clan's integrity—even Zhu Yun and Ji An cannot be looked up to!"

literal: Shao said, "I only regret that the execution came somewhat late—that is my shame."
idiomatic: Shao said, "I only regret that the execution came somewhat late—that is my shame."

literal: He died as Inspector of Liang Province.
idiomatic: He died as Inspector of Liang Province.

literal: Peijin's younger brother Zhong, styled Xiande, was known for loyalty and prudence.
idiomatic: Peijin's younger brother Zhong, styled Xiande, was known for loyalty and prudence.

literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was repeatedly promoted to Right Deputy, enfeoffed Duke of Chengyang, added Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Guards the West; he had merit in assisting and supporting—all officials respected him.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was repeatedly promoted to Right Deputy, enfeoffed Duke of Chengyang, added Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Guards the West; he had merit in assisting and supporting—all officials respected him.

literal: In the fourth year of Taihe, gravely ill he declined office; he nursed illness at Gaoliu; the imperial carriage personally escorted him beyond the capital gate; attending ministers who took leave—none did not weep.
idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe, gravely ill he declined office; he nursed illness at Gaoliu; the imperial carriage personally escorted him beyond the capital gate; attending ministers who took leave—none did not weep.

literal: When he died, all mourned and regretted him.
idiomatic: When he died, all mourned and regretted him.

literal: Posthumous title Xuan; an order was given that the authorities erect a stele inscription.
idiomatic: Posthumous title Xuan; an order was given that the authorities erect a stele inscription.

literal: Son Sheng, styled Shixing, inherited the title, post Master of Ceremonies.
idiomatic: Son Sheng, styled Shixing, inherited the title, post Master of Ceremonies.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Son Mao, styled Boyong, inherited the title, demoted to marquis.
idiomatic: Son Mao, styled Boyong, inherited the title, demoted to marquis.

literal: Following the emperor into Guanzhong, he was enfeoffed Prince of Beiping.
idiomatic: Following the emperor into Guanzhong, he was enfeoffed Prince of Beiping.

literal: He died; posthumously Minister of the Secretariat Left Deputy, posthumous title Zhenhui.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously Minister of the Secretariat Left Deputy, posthumous title Zhenhui.

literal: Son Zhi, styled Jingsheng, Grand Guardian with seals equal to the Three Dukes.
idiomatic: Son Zhi, styled Jingsheng, Grand Guardian with seals equal to the Three Dukes.

literal: Younger brother Shun, styled Jingshu, followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong, enfeoffed Prince of Puyang, post Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: Younger brother Shun, styled Jingshu, followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong, enfeoffed Prince of Puyang, post Attendant-in-Ordinary.

literal: When Emperor Wu died, the mourning was kept secret unannounced; many proposed Prince of Guangping as successor.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu died, the mourning was kept secret unannounced; many proposed Prince of Guangping as successor.

literal: Shun in a side room wept and said to Zhou Wen, "Guangping though kin is advanced in years and virtue—he should not occupy the great treasure."
idiomatic: Shun in a side room wept and said to Zhou Wen, "Guangping though kin is advanced in years and virtue—he should not occupy the great treasure."

literal: Zhou Wen deeply agreed; he thereupon proclaimed the national taboo and elevated the Prince of Nanyang to the imperial title.
idiomatic: Zhou Wen deeply agreed; he thereupon proclaimed the national taboo and elevated the Prince of Nanyang to the imperial title.

literal: Shun was made Commandant, acting Yong Province affairs, and also added Grand Guardian with seals equal to the Three Dukes and Inspector of Qin Province.
idiomatic: Shun was made Commandant, acting Yong Province affairs, and also added Grand Guardian with seals equal to the Three Dukes and Inspector of Qin Province.

literal: Shun was skilled at archery.
idiomatic: Shun was skilled at archery.

literal: At first, when Emperor Xiaowu was at Luoyang, in Huayin Garden he amused himself with shooting; a silver wine goblet holding about two sheng was hung a hundred paces away; he ordered a dozen skilled archers to shoot together—whoever hit received it as gift.
idiomatic: At first, when Emperor Xiaowu was at Luoyang, in Huayin Garden he amused himself with shooting; a silver wine goblet holding about two sheng was hung a hundred paces away; he ordered a dozen skilled archers to shoot together—whoever hit received it as gift.

literal: Shun loosed an arrow and at once hit; the emperor was greatly pleased and rewarded him with gold and silk together.
idiomatic: Shun loosed an arrow and at once hit; the emperor was greatly pleased and rewarded him with gold and silk together.

literal: Shun then at the arrow-hole cast a silver boy treading a golden lotus, holding skewered roast in hand, and had it inscribed on the back, recording his archery.
idiomatic: Shun then at the arrow-hole cast a silver boy treading a golden lotus, holding skewered roast in hand, and had it inscribed on the back, recording his archery.

literal: Son Wei, styled Ziyou, had pure talent.
idiomatic: Son Wei, styled Ziyou, had pure talent.

literal: In the sixteenth year of Datong he was enfeoffed Prince of Nan'an Commandery.
idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Datong he was enfeoffed Prince of Nan'an Commandery.

literal: When Yuchi Jiong campaigned against Shu, Wei was made Registrar; the documents and proclamations were all Wei's work.
idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong campaigned against Shu, Wei was made Registrar; the documents and proclamations were all Wei's work.

literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Master of the Mentorate Lower Grand Master, changed to Duke of Huainan county.
idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Master of the Mentorate Lower Grand Master, changed to Duke of Huainan county.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming of Zhou he was Master of the Mentorate Middle Grand Master and received an edict at Qilin Hall to collate the canonical texts.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming of Zhou he was Master of the Mentorate Middle Grand Master and received an edict at Qilin Hall to collate the canonical texts.

literal: In the Jiande era he was repeatedly promoted to Junior Minister of Justice, made envoy chief, and returned courtesy to Qi.
idiomatic: In the Jiande era he was repeatedly promoted to Junior Minister of Justice, made envoy chief, and returned courtesy to Qi.

literal: That autumn the Emperor Wu personally led the eastern campaign; Wei was then detained by Qi.
idiomatic: That autumn the Emperor Wu personally led the eastern campaign; Wei was then detained by Qi.

literal: When Qi was pacified, Wei was at last released and additionally granted Upper Opening of the Office.
idiomatic: When Qi was pacified, Wei was at last released and additionally granted Upper Opening of the Office.

literal: Later he was made Inspector of Xiang Province, post Grand General.
idiomatic: Later he was made Inspector of Xiang Province, post Grand General.

literal: Wei was gentle by nature, loved quiet and emptiness, studied deeply and loved literature.
idiomatic: Wei was gentle by nature, loved quiet and emptiness, studied deeply and loved literature.

literal: When he first returned from Ye, Yu Xin presented him a poem saying, "Liang perished and Chuiji returned; Qi was pacified and the precious tripod came home."
idiomatic: When he first returned from Ye, Yu Xin presented him a poem saying, "Liang perished and Chuiji returned; Qi was pacified and the precious tripod came home."

literal: Thus he was valued by men of letters.
idiomatic: Thus he was valued by men of letters.

literal: Later he died of illness.
idiomatic: Later he died of illness.

literal: Sheng's younger brother Shouxing was clever from youth and loved learning.
idiomatic: Sheng's younger brother Shouxing was clever from youth and loved learning.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu he was Inspector of Xu Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu he was Inspector of Xu Province.

literal: In office he was greedy and cruel, failing in men's hearts.
idiomatic: In office he was greedy and cruel, failing in men's hearts.

literal: His cousin the Attendant-in-Ordinary Hui deeply feared his ability and therefore slandered him to the emperor; an edict ordered Minister of the Secretariat Cui Liang to gallop post-horses and inspect.
idiomatic: His cousin the Attendant-in-Ordinary Hui deeply feared his ability and therefore slandered him to the emperor; an edict ordered Minister of the Secretariat Cui Liang to gallop post-horses and inspect.

literal: On the day Liang set out he received Hui's instruction; he thereupon flogged three widows and made them falsely confess that Shouxing had pressed them into bondage as maidservants.
idiomatic: On the day Liang set out he received Hui's instruction; he thereupon flogged three widows and made them falsely confess that Shouxing had pressed them into bondage as maidservants.

literal: Shouxing in the end feared he could not escape; he therefore ordered his wife's younger brother Central Army Commander Xue Xiuyi to take ten carts and transport wheat, passing by his place of detention.
idiomatic: Shouxing in the end feared he could not escape; he therefore ordered his wife's younger brother Central Army Commander Xue Xiuyi to take ten carts and transport wheat, passing by his place of detention.

literal: Shouxing then climbed the wall and fled; Xiuyi with a great wooden chest enclosed Shouxing, wheat heaped above, and carried him out; he reached Hedong and hid in Xiuyi's house.
idiomatic: Shouxing then climbed the wall and fled; Xiuyi with a great wooden chest enclosed Shouxing, wheat heaped above, and carried him out; he reached Hedong and hid in Xiuyi's house.

literal: Meeting an amnesty he came out, saw the emperor, and himself stated he was slandered by Hui; the emperor also had nothing further to reproach.
idiomatic: Meeting an amnesty he came out, saw the emperor, and himself stated he was slandered by Hui; the emperor also had nothing further to reproach.

literal: At first, when Shouxing was Junior Mentor, Wang Xian was in the Eastern Palace.
idiomatic: At first, when Shouxing was Junior Mentor, Wang Xian was in the Eastern Palace.

literal: When low in rank, for public business Shouxing caned him forty strokes.
idiomatic: When low in rank, for public business Shouxing caned him forty strokes.

literal: When Xian had favor, as Imperial Censor he memorialized that Shouxing at home often had resentful words and slandered the court.
idiomatic: When Xian had favor, as Imperial Censor he memorialized that Shouxing at home often had resentful words and slandered the court.

literal: Because the emperor drank to excess without awareness, he thereupon memorialized the matter; the emperor was ordered to annotate approval and it was sent straight to Shouxing to be granted death.
idiomatic: Because the emperor drank to excess without awareness, he thereupon memorialized the matter; the emperor was ordered to annotate approval and it was sent straight to Shouxing to be granted death.

literal: The emperor's writing was half incomplete characters; those who saw at the time also knew it was not his true heart—yet they feared Hui and others' power and dared not speak in rescue.
idiomatic: The emperor's writing was half incomplete characters; those who saw at the time also knew it was not his true heart—yet they feared Hui and others' power and dared not speak in rescue.

literal: On the day of execution Xian himself went to watch.
idiomatic: On the day of execution Xian himself went to watch.

literal: Shouxing ordered brush and himself composed his tomb inscription: "A Luoyang man, surname Yuan given name Jing, had the Way but not the time—his years not long."
idiomatic: Shouxing ordered brush and himself composed his tomb inscription: "A Luoyang man, surname Yuan given name Jing, had the Way but not the time—his years not long."

literal: The remaining text is mostly not recorded.
idiomatic: The remaining text is mostly not recorded.

literal: He looked at his son and said, "In my coffin place a hundred sheets of paper and two brushes—I wish to sue Xian in the underworld.
idiomatic: He looked at his son and said, "In my coffin place a hundred sheets of paper and two brushes—I wish to sue Xian in the underworld.

literal: If the High Ancestor's spirit has knowledge, within a hundred days he will surely take Xian.
idiomatic: If the High Ancestor's spirit has knowledge, within a hundred days he will surely take Xian.

literal: If in the end there is no knowledge, what is there to cherish!"
idiomatic: If in the end there is no knowledge, what is there to cherish!"

literal: When Emperor Xuanwu died, Xian was soon killed.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu died, Xian was soon killed.

literal: Shouxing's death—opinion of the time also held that the former Commandant's impeachment of Gao Que's slander and satire had caused it.
idiomatic: Shouxing's death—opinion of the time also held that the former Commandant's impeachment of Gao Que's slander and satire had caused it.

literal: When Empress Ling held court, Third Excellency Bureau Attendant Cui Hong memorialized to clear Shouxing; an edict pursued vindication, posthumously Inspector of Yu Province, posthumous title Zhuang.
idiomatic: When Empress Ling held court, Third Excellency Bureau Attendant Cui Hong memorialized to clear Shouxing; an edict pursued vindication, posthumously Inspector of Yu Province, posthumous title Zhuang.

literal: Son Zui, styled Gan, followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong, enfeoffed Prince of Leping, post Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Minister of the Secretariat Left Deputy, specially advanced.
idiomatic: Son Zui, styled Gan, followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong, enfeoffed Prince of Leping, post Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Minister of the Secretariat Left Deputy, specially advanced.

literal: Shouxing's younger brother Yisheng died young.
idiomatic: Shouxing's younger brother Yisheng died young.

literal: Zhong's younger brother De was enfeoffed Duke of Hejian, died as General Who Guards the South, posthumously Inspector of Cao Province.
idiomatic: Zhong's younger brother De was enfeoffed Duke of Hejian, died as General Who Guards the South, posthumously Inspector of Cao Province.

literal: De's son Ti, Yingchuan Administrator, died as Inspector of Guang Province, posthumous title Gong.
idiomatic: De's son Ti, Yingchuan Administrator, died as Inspector of Guang Province, posthumous title Gong.

literal: Ti's younger brother Hui, styled Jingxi.
idiomatic: Ti's younger brother Hui, styled Jingxi.

literal: From youth deep and keen, he quite traversed literature and history.
idiomatic: From youth deep and keen, he quite traversed literature and history.

literal: When Emperor Xuanwu took the throne he was Attendant Who Attends to Affairs as Yellow Gate Attendant.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu took the throne he was Attendant Who Attends to Affairs as Yellow Gate Attendant.

literal: At first when Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, the old nobility all found it hard to shift; then wishing to harmonize popular feeling, he permitted winter dwelling in the south and summer dwelling in the north.
idiomatic: At first when Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, the old nobility all found it hard to shift; then wishing to harmonize popular feeling, he permitted winter dwelling in the south and summer dwelling in the north.

literal: Emperor Xuanwu was quite misled by words of those at his side; outsiders then had questions of returning north.
idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu was quite misled by words of those at his side; outsiders then had questions of returning north.

literal: It reached the point of posting notices selling fields and houses, not at ease in their dwellings.
idiomatic: It reached the point of posting notices selling fields and houses, not at ease in their dwellings.
